input.question: Why does a hearing a recording of my voice sound different to me then when I hear myself talk?
input.ground_truth: We hear sounds as vibrations hitting our ear drums. When we hear most sounds, these vibrations travel through the air and into the ear canal. Our own voices also vibrate through our bodies, creating a slightly lower pitch. When you hear a recording of your voice you are missing this extra level of vibration that lowers the sound, so your voice sounds higher than what you are used to. Source: _URL_0_

Answer:

response.prediction: When you hear your own voice while speaking, most of the sound reaches your ears through the bones of your skull and through the tissues of your head and neck. This makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself. However, when you listen to a recording, the sound reaches your ears only through the air, just like how others hear it. This version of your voice usually sounds higher and thinner because it lacks the vibrations conducted through your bones. That’s why your recorded voice can sound different from what you expect when you speak.
